description: How much organization a piece of work gets. The department cycle is correct and it is not free: worker, self-check, peer review, lead review, rollup, acceptance is the right shape for a novel change to a coupled surface and pure overhead for a one-line correction to a document nobody depends on. Intensity selects a path through the cycle that already exists. It does not create four cycles.
what_this_is_not: Not a way to skip independent review. Intensity controls the depth applied to one task; the department cycle's own acceptance conditions still require an independent verdict on the department's output, and no level changes them. A MICRO task rolls up into a cycle that gets peer-reviewed as a whole.
Not a discount for risky work. Every floor below raises intensity and none lowers it, so the signals can only ever add ceremony to work that turns out to need it.
Not a judgement about the worker. A MICRO task is a small task, not a trusted one.

MICRO.means: The worker does it and validates it. Nobody else looks at this task on its own; the department's output is still reviewed before the cycle is accepted.
MICRO.use_when: A change whose failure mode is visible in the work itself: a document correction, a recorded skip, a discovery step that produces no artifact anyone depends on.

STANDARD.means: An independent peer reads it. The lead does not re-review what the peer already read.
STANDARD.use_when: The ordinary case. Anything producing an artifact another stage consumes.

COMPLEX.means: Peer review for detail, lead review for adherence and integration, and the rollup the head reads.
COMPLEX.use_when: Work the lead has to integrate with other work, or that changes a shape the department owns.

adds: the human approval its stage names, which no agent verdict satisfies
CRITICAL.means: Everything COMPLEX has, and the governance the approval policy requires. The depth is not the point here; the named human is.
CRITICAL.use_when: CRITICAL risk, production mutation, a security or authorization boundary, an irreversible act.
CRITICAL.cost: Highest, and correct. This level exists so the others can be cheaper without argument.

why_the_default_is_standard: A default of MICRO makes every unconsidered task unreviewed, and a default of COMPLEX makes the model pay for a lead on work nobody needs to integrate. STANDARD is the level whose absence is a real gap and whose presence is rarely waste.

signals.reads: the task's risk, or its stage's
signals.effect: CRITICAL risk forces CRITICAL. HIGH raises the floor to COMPLEX.
signals.why: Risk is the organization's own statement about what failure costs, made before the work started. Letting a later signal lower it would make the tier decorative.

signals.reads: the stage's declared complexity: routine, complex or novel
signals.effect: novel raises the floor to COMPLEX. routine permits MICRO where nothing else objects.
signals.why: Novel work is where a lead's integration view is worth most, because nobody has done it before and the shape is still being decided.

signals.reads: whether the stage deploys, promotes, migrates or authorizes
signals.why: Ceremony after the fact is not review. The only place depth is worth its cost unconditionally is where the change cannot be taken back.

signals.effect: incident, release and migration raise the floor to COMPLEX.
signals.why: These are the three types where the cost of being wrong is paid by somebody other than the author, and where the lead's integration view is the whole point.

signals.reads: whether the task holds a coupled surface, per policies/coupling-policy.json
signals.why: A coupled surface has one owner and several consumers. The review that matters is the one that sees the consumers, which is the lead's.

signals.reads: the number of predicates in the task's definition of done
signals.effect: a task with more than six predicates cannot be MICRO.
signals.why: A proxy, and named as one. Predicate count is not size; it is the only size-shaped number available before the work is done, and it is a floor rather than a ceiling so a wrong reading costs ceremony rather than review.

signals.reads: whether the task names a reviewer, or its definition of done contains agent_verdict
signals.why: The mechanical one. A definition of done that demands an independent verdict cannot be satisfied by a path that has nobody produce one, so MICRO is not merely discouraged here -- it is unreachable, and the predicate would refuse it anyway.

signals.reads: whether the stage names a human approval, or its definition of done contains human_approval_recorded
signals.why: Work a named human has to approve is not work the organization was treating as trivial.

resolution.rule: Start at the stage's declared intensity or the default. Apply every signal. Each one can only raise. The result is the highest floor any signal set.
resolution.why_only_raise: A model choosing how much review its own work gets is the failure this policy would otherwise introduce. Signals that could lower would make the level an argument; signals that only raise make it an observation.
resolution.resolved_by: scripts/resolve_intensity.py, at plan time, and again on any replan.
resolution.recorded_on: the task's `intensity` field, as declared and resolved, with the signal that set it.

invariants: No level removes a definition-of-done predicate. Intensity chooses who looks at the work, never what the work has to satisfy.
No level changes the department cycle's acceptance conditions. A MICRO task still belongs to a cycle whose output is independently reviewed before it is accepted.
MICRO is unreachable for any task whose definition of done contains agent_verdict or human_approval_recorded. The predicate refuses it, so the policy and the checker cannot disagree.
CRITICAL risk always resolves to CRITICAL, whatever else is true.
An agent never chooses its own intensity. It is resolved from facts at plan time and recorded.
not_enforceable: Nothing makes an agent actually perform the review the level requires. The cycle states are a contract the model follows; what is mechanical is the acceptance condition at the end, which fails if the verdict it wants was never recorded.
Task size is read from predicate count, which is a proxy. A large task with a short definition of done reads as small.
Reversibility is inferred from what the stage does, not from what the change actually touches. A migration stage that only adds a nullable column is treated as irreversible.
